Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Vertex Petroleum Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Vertex Petroleum Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; and Tom Reilly, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Vertex Petroleum delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production levels and meaningful progress across our key priorities. I'm particularly pleased with our advancements in future development plans, where we're positioning our high-quality inventory for sustained growth amid WTI above $80 and Brent near $85. We're also executing aggressively on ESG initiatives, including emissions reductions that are ahead of targets, while maintaining exemplary environmental performance with zero major incidents. Disciplined capital allocation has kept us under budget, ensuring robust free cash flow generation. We remain focused on high-return oil-weighted development, cost efficiencies, and responsible operations to drive long-term shareholder value.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $1.25 billion, up 28% year-over-year, reflecting higher production volumes and realized pricing of $78 per barrel equivalent. Operating income was $480 million, up 35%, and net income came in at $350 million, or $1.85 per diluted share. We generated $380 million in free cash flow and returned $180 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $2.4 billion in long-term debt and $950 million in cash and equivalents, providing ample liquidity for our growth plans.

Before moving to operations, I'd like to highlight our capital expenditure performance and environmental track record, as these underscore our commitment to efficiency and sustainability. Starting with capex, we continue to demonstrate strong cost discipline in a volatile macro environment. WTI crude is holding steady around $82 per barrel, but service cost inflation—up about 8% year-over-year based on benchmarking against peers like Pioneer and Occidental—has pressured the sector. That said, Vertex delivered total capex of $295 million in Q3, 11% under our $330 million quarterly budget, or $1.08 billion year-to-date against our $1.25 billion full-year guidance midpoint. This under-spend sets us up nicely to accelerate high-return projects in Q4 without needing additional capital.

Let me detail this by category: drilling, completion, and facilities, including budget versus actuals and the drivers.

Drilling came in at $122 million actual versus a $145 million budget, 16% under due to multi-well pad efficiencies and tech advancements. We spudded 25 operated wells against a plan for 23, leveraging our partnership with Helmerich & Payne's FlexRig fleet. Days per 1-mile lateral improved to 14 days from 16.5 in Q2, thanks to rotary steerable systems and PDC bits from Schlumberger. This cut AFE costs by $4.8 million per pad in our Delaware Basin focus area, where Permian drilling represented 93% of activity. Eagle Ford saw some weather-related delays, but we're pacing 12% ahead year-to-date, with deferrals on lower-tier tests preserving premium inventory.

Completions were $135 million actual against $125 million budgeted, a 8% overrun from proppant and chemistry inflation—sand up 14% on rail constraints from the Wisconsin basin, similar to reports from EOG and Devon. We turned in line 30 wells versus 26 planned, with 50 stages per well and 2,300 lbs/ft proppant intensity to lift EURs 16%. Highlights included 'super-zipper' fracs on Delaware pads, cutting cycle times 22% to 44 days spud-to-TIL, and slickwater designs mitigating parent-child effects. Gulf tie-backs added modestly but deliver $26 per BOE LOE. Year-to-date, we're just 2% over budget, with Q4 fixed-price deals from Halliburton to cap risks.

Facilities spend was $38 million versus $60 million planned, 37% under, from strategic deferrals on non-essentials. Permian water infrastructure took $22 million to hit 87% recycle targets next year, while $18 million in compression and gathering shifted to Q1 amid EPC tightness post-hurricanes. We commissioned a $13 million produced water facility with vapor recovery, dropping flaring 42% year-over-year. Offshore deferrals on TLP upgrades await FID on extensions with strong IRRs. Year-to-date facilities are 25% under, fueling bolt-on opportunities like our recent $60 million Delaware add.

Overall, $35 million Q3 savings boost free cash flow toward $500 million full-year at strip, with 65% returns via buybacks and dividends. FY24 capex stays $1.2-$1.3 billion, 72% D&C for 48,000 BOE/d new production.

Shifting to environmental performance, ESG is integral to our operations—beyond compliance, it's about excellence, efficiency, and our license to operate amid net-zero demands. We've outperformed internal targets and API/IOGP benchmarks. Q3 saw zero Tier 1 incidents—events with major offsite potential like spills over 5 barrels. Year-to-date, three reportable spills totaled 7 barrels of hydrocarbons, down 70% from 23 barrels last year and 85% from our five-year 48-barrel average. Spill frequency rate is 0.11 per million production days, beating API's 0.34 and our 0.18 target.

Details: Two small crude releases under 3 barrels from Permian gathering lines due to third-party corrosion; one 4-barrel produced water during Eagle Ford flowback, berm-contained. No waterway or habitat impacts. Total incident rate, including near-misses, is 0.42 per million hours, down 28% year-over-year via 'Zero Harm.'

By region: Permian (62% production) had zero hydrocarbon spills in Q3—first since our 2022 Delaware acquisition—thanks to pad optimization and electrified water systems cutting spill sources 45%. Volumes down 60% year-over-year. Gulf platforms spill-free with ROV integrity and acoustic detection exceeding BOEM SEMS II. North Sea JVs one minor <1 liter chemical release, remediated onsite per OSPAR.

Remediation: 99% hydrocarbon recovery via absorbents, vacuum, bioremediation. Sites stabilized in 3.5 hours under our 8-hour KPI, closed in 40 days. All 2023 legacies done, including a 16-barrel Permian overflow with chemical oxidation and VOC sensors. Spend $4.5 million within $16 million budget, no reserve hit. Savings: 14% insurance discount from AIG, $9 million avoided fines.

Tech drivers: Fiber-optic DAS/DTS on 1,300 Permian pipeline miles with OptaSense flags issues 72 hours early, averting 17 barrels. AI predictive maintenance via Schlumberger Delfi and drone LiDAR cuts leak risks 38%. Autonomous PIGs with Baker Hughes in Gulf hit 99.9% ILI. 88% sites ISO 14001, on track for SBTi with spill ties to 28% methane cut by 2025.

This is strategic: $800 million five-year digital/green capex (11% upstream). Low incidents de-risk $2.2 billion Permian CO2-EOR, attract ESG funds with 18% JV premiums. Q4 steady, 'Spill Zero' AI ahead.

I will now turn the call over to Tom Reilly for an operational update.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Maria. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 295,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 12% year-over-year, with 70% oil. We successfully brought the Olympus field tie-back online in the Gulf of Mexico, ramping to 20,000 boe/d ahead of schedule and expected to contribute meaningfully to growth in coming quarters. Cost reduction initiatives are yielding results: LOE down 8% to $8.50 per boe through water recycling and vendor partnerships, while our drilling efficiencies have compressed breakevens to $38 per barrel. We're advancing ESG-aligned ops like electrified rigs and methane monitoring across 90% of assets, tying directly to emissions progress.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning team. Johnathan, could you walk us through your future development plans and resource potential? Specifically, how you're positioning the portfolio amid the current macro with WTI holding above $80 and Brent at $85, and any updates on D&C inventory quality?

Johnathan Hale: Absolutely, Sarah, great question and timely as we just wrapped up our Q3 reserve report with Netherland, Sewell & Associates. Let me dive into this—breaking it down by core regions, technical initiatives, capex framework, and upside levers. We're laser-focused on high-return, oil-weighted inventory to drive free cash flow through the cycle, layering in disciplined M&A and tech to extend our runway.

High-level: Year-end 2023 proved developed producing reserves at 870 MMboe on 1P, 2P at 1.85 Bboe, 3P to 3.3 Bboe—up 17% year-over-year from Permian EUR gains and Gulf tie-backs. Drilling inventory over 6,400 gross D&C locations, 4,700 net to VPI—more than 16 years runway. NPV10 pre-tax on 2P is $29 billion at $70 flat WTI, uplifting 22% to $36 billion at strip.

Permian, 67% capex: 2.9 million net acres Delaware/Midland, core 400 ft spacing. 2P unrisked 1.25 Bboe net, 3P adds 850 MMboe from SALT-3/Woodford. 2025-2027: 260 wells/year, 18,500-foot laterals, hyper-cube fracs—125 stages, 4,700 lbs/ft slickwater hybrids. Permian EURs now 1.45 Mboe/well, up 27% YoY; drilling $7.3 million from $9.5 million 2022. Declines 64% year-one via parent-child models, fiber diagnostics, AI fracs—Exxon-Pioneer style.

Eagle Ford, 22% slate: 1.15 Bboe 2P on 470,000 net acres Karnes/DeWitt. 58% oil/condensate for Mont Belvieu. 85 wells 2025, Black Hawk window, 12,500-ft laterals, dissolvable diverters. Costs <$5.8 million/well, IRRs >65% at $70. CO2 EOR pilot Pearsall unlocks 320 MMboe, Occidental-like.

International 13%: GoM shelf 125,000 net acres, 470 MMboe 2P Olympus subsalt—FID Q2 2025, $520 million tie-back to Thunder Horse, Chevron Anchor-style. Ramp 26,000 boe/d 2027, 77% liquids. Appalachia Marcellus/Utica 370 Bcf 2P, LNG upside; EQT JV 105,000 acres, 160 pads electrified, Scope 1 cut 42%.

Tech: $160 million R&D—ML seismic de-risks 32% more Tier 1, 99% success. Rigless perf/electric fracs 45% fleet, breakevens $34-44/bbl. ESG: Net-zero Scope 1/2 2035, $220 million CCUS decade, Oxy hubs, 82% Permian renewables.

Capex 2025 $2.9-3.1 billion, 76% D&C, 11-13% growth to 330,000 boe/d, 69% oil. FCF yield 19% strip, dividends 2.2x. Bolt-ons $1.2-2.2 billion for 550 locations, Chord-Yellowstone style. Tailwinds: OPEC+ cuts, LNG +27% Shell LTG, $16/bbl cracks.

Risks: volatility, regs, services—but top-quartile like Conoco or EOG. Follow-ups welcome.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Energy Insights. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning, team. I wanted to dive into your ESG initiatives, particularly progress on emissions reduction targets. With the recent IEA report highlighting upstream methane as a key lever for Paris alignment, can you update us on Scope 1 and 2 progress, any regional nuances, and how this ties into your LDAR and CCUS ramps?

Maria Gonzalez: Good morning, Sarah—great question, timely with SEC climate rules and EU CBAM. At Vertex, emissions reductions are core to value creation. Against 2030 targets: 42% absolute Scope 1/2 cut from 2019 47 million tCO2e baseline, net-zero ops 2050—we're ahead.

Q3 Scope 1/2: 8.4 million tCO2e, down 24% YoY, 20% sequential. Intensity 13.8 kg CO2e/boe on 1.85 million boe/d base, 27% YoY drop from 18.9—below IOGP 19 average, Occidental-tier.

Scopes: 1 down 30% to 7.1 Mt (methane/flaring); 2 down 14% to 1.3 Mt (grid/renewables). Scope 3 ~155 Mt, 17% to 27% intensity cut via suppliers/low-carbon premiums.

Initiatives:

Methane: Continuous monitors 88% assets (GHGSat satellites, FLIR drone OGI)—intensity 0.16% gross gas from 0.32% 2022, ahead 0.18% target. Permian 460,000 boe/d: 78% pneumatic swaps to electronic, save $16 million gas, capture 1.3 Bcf/d sales.

Flaring: <0.8% total gas, World Bank pledge. Q3 0.4% disposed, down 2.4% YoY—VRUs, electrified compressors. Bakken 97% to Enterprise JV.

Electrification: 43% GoM platforms grid via Entergy, cut NOx/CO2 160,000 tons. Onshore Baker Hughes Jewel AI: 14% fuel cut 5,200 wells. Guyana subsea Yellowtail/Exxon minimizes venting.

CCUS: Permian Hub (Oxy/Chevron) 5.2 Mtpa 2027, Q2 injection 0.6 Mtpa, 45Q $52/ton. Norway/Equinor Sleipner 1.1 Mtpa Northern Lights.

Regions:

US Onshore (67%): Permian/Bakken 32% intensity cuts, DOE grants, 100% electric rigs vs. GORs.

GoM (18%): 11.5 kg/boe, TLP/Shell blue H2.

Intl (15%): Norway 7.5 kg/boe hydro; Brazil pre-salt 20 kg/boe FPSO—$220 million 2025 CCUS, Petrobras ties.

Accretive: $130 million 2024 gas sales/fine avoids, 6-12% RSG premium MiQ to Amazon. 9% $4.7 billion 2025 capex ($420 million) low-carbon, IRR>22%. Q4 22-27% YoY cut, S&P ESG, green bonds 55 bps tight.

TCFD report soon. More on Scope 3 audits?

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Thompson with Global Energy Research. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson: Good morning. Could you provide more color on how your cost reduction initiatives are impacting breakevens and any updates on new well performance?

Tom Reilly: Good morning, Mike. Our initiatives are delivering across the board. LOE efficiencies from water management and vendor renegotiations have full-cycle breakevens at $36-42 per barrel in the Permian, with half-cycle under $30. New Olympus wells are outperforming type curve by 15% initial rates, thanks to optimized completions. We're applying similar learnings onshore, with Eagle Ford pads hitting 1.2 Mboe EURs ahead of plan.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy—high-grading inventory, driving operational excellence, advancing ESG and environmental leadership, and delivering value to our shareholders through free cash flow and returns. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
